findings.text: sre lens, medium: Four new lines pipe grep's output into head -1, which exits early once it reads one line; under set -euo pipefail, grep takes SIGPIPE when call-sequence has more entries than head reads, causing the pipeline to exit non-zero inside the subshell — the assignment gets an empty string and the ordering assertions silently pass or fail on a blank. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/tests/claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh: "_post_line="$(/usr/bin/grep -n "^POST_NOTE$" "$GHS/call-sequence" | /usr/bin/head -1 | cut -d: -f1)""; happens when: Any future test scenario that calls claim_coordinator_claim twice without resetting GHS (so POST_NOTE appears more than once in call-sequence), or a parallel test runner that appends to call-sequence concurrently.; fix: test; ACCEPTED IF: the four ordering-line extractions use a form that cannot receive SIGPIPE — grep directly against the file with a line-number, captured in full and trimmed in bash, or a here-string — rather than piping grep into head; and the sigpipe guard's | head scan, which now excludes -test.sh files, covers this test file or the test carries a sigpipe-ok annotation with a stated reason.); the same kind of problem also at: plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/tests/claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh | _get_line="$(/usr/bin/grep -n "^GET_NOTES$" "$GHS/call-sequence" | /usr/bin/head -1 | cut -d: -f1)"; plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/tests/claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh | _post_line="$(/usr/bin/grep -n "^POST_NOTE$" "$GHS/call-sequence" | /usr/bin/head -1 | cut -d: -f1)"; plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/tests/claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh | _get_line="$(/usr/bin/grep -n "^GET_NOTES$" "$GHS/call-sequence" | /usr/bin/head -1 | cut -d: -f1)"
